plugins.name: design-workflow
plugins.description: Interview the user into implementable workflow specifications for recurring loops in their work, using the current directory as a stateful workspace.

plugins.name: guide
plugins.description: Choose the next skill, development workflow, or session boundary from the current situation.

plugins.name: hand-off
plugins.description: Write the current session's work into a versioned, self-contained handoff document in .agents/handoffs/ and point to it from AGENTS.md, so another session, agent, or person can resume it.

plugins.name: illustrate
plugins.description: Explain the current topic visually.

plugins.name: memorize
plugins.description: File a lesson in the home the next agent will read, and recall saved scripts and lessons before redoing work.

plugins.name: optimize-process
plugins.description: Analyze and improve a recurring work process when the user reports delays, excessive steps, rework, or handoff friction.

plugins.name: publish-message
plugins.description: Publish an established conclusion or review summary to a connected service (code host, tracker, chat, documentation, email) in its conventions.

plugins.name: re-explain
plugins.description: Re-explain what did not land, with the missing context and familiar vocabulary.

plugins.name: swarm
plugins.description: Divide one task into independent pieces and run them in parallel on fast, low-cost subagents the user selects, then merge and spot-check their reports.

plugins.name: teach
plugins.description: Teach the user a skill or concept over multiple sessions in a stateful workspace.

plugins.name: unslop
plugins.description: Cut AI tells from prose that other people will read, in any language.

plugins.name: walk-through
plugins.description: Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform.

plugins.name: write-for-agents
plugins.description: Write documents for agents: skills, AGENTS.md, and documents reached by a pointer.

plugins.name: codify
plugins.description: Define the project's code conventions by drafting candidate rules from how the code is already written and confirming each with the user and its reason, or audit an existing conventions file.

plugins.name: setup-ai-tooling
plugins.description: Set up free AI development tools for a project and its installed agent clients.

plugins.name: setup-ai-workspace
plugins.description: Configure a repository for AI-assisted work: task tracking, ticket conventions, and triage roles.

plugins.name: setup-delegation-policy
plugins.description: Install the delegation and model routing rule into the global steering files on this machine.

plugins.name: setup-git-guardrails
plugins.description: Set up hooks and permission rules that make coding agents ask before git commands that can lose work or rewrite shared history (pushing to a protected branch, force pushes, reset --hard, clean -f, branch -D, discarding changes) across Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex CLI.

plugins.name: setup-git-hooks
plugins.description: Set up versioned git hooks via core.hooksPath (no Husky) with lint-staged (Biome, plus Prettier only for languages Biome leaves uncovered and only if the user wants it), plus typecheck and build.

plugins.name: graphify
plugins.description: Build and work through a shared decision graph for an effort too large for one session.

plugins.name: interview
plugins.description: Interview the user in rounds of questions, each with a recommended answer, until a plan, decision, or idea is settled.

plugins.name: prioritize
plugins.description: Decompose a large or tangled idea into outcomes, recommend one focus to build next, and keep the rest in the backlog.

plugins.name: prototype
plugins.description: Build a scoped experimental prototype to answer a user-requested or approved design question about logic, state, or UI.

plugins.name: research
plugins.description: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repository.

plugins.name: debug
plugins.description: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions.

plugins.name: improve-codebase-architecture
plugins.description: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then interview through the chosen one.

plugins.name: improve-environment
plugins.description: Hold a retrospective on a session's friction, then change the project's environment so the next run avoids it: checks, guardrails, navigation pointers, steering files, tool and information access.

plugins.name: improve-skills
plugins.description: Hold a retrospective on a session, then report how the skills behaved as an issue on the skills repository.

plugins.name: monitor-ai-tooling
plugins.description: Report AI tooling usage, measured output reduction, quality signals, and gaps from existing local measurements.

plugins.name: triage
plugins.description: Move tasks and external PRs through triage roles: categorize, verify, refine, and write agent-ready briefs.

plugins.name: draft-merge-request
plugins.description: Write the body of a pull request or merge request: a summary visual, before/after evidence, and the merge danger.

plugins.name: rebase
plugins.description: Rebase local branches in place onto one target, resolve conflicts, run checks, then push with force-with-lease on approval.

plugins.name: resolve-merge-conflicts
plugins.description: Resolve an in-progress git merge or rebase conflict.

plugins.name: sync-tree
plugins.description: Sync a completed Git worktree branch to its corresponding branch in the original local repository.

plugins.name: work-in-tree
plugins.description: Create or reuse an isolated Git worktree and carry out the task there, preserving the original checkout.

plugins.name: address-feedback
plugins.description: Assess review feedback from any source (pull or merge request, issue, ticket, document comments, pasted notes), propose dispositions, then implement and reply.

plugins.name: architect
plugins.description: Decide or assess a system's technical shape (technology stack, parts and their boundaries, data ownership and flows, integrations, deployment) and how it meets the system-wide requirements, weighing alternatives and their tradeoffs.

plugins.name: delineate
plugins.description: Outline a system functionally (its purpose, actors, domain contexts, capability map, system-wide requirements, and glossary), settling fuzzy or conflicting terms along the way.

plugins.name: divide-and-conquer
plugins.description: Implement an authorized task graph in parallel: route each task to the least expensive capable agent, build on one integration branch, then review once.

plugins.name: engineer
plugins.description: Design one capability's technical solution before implementation (modules and their interfaces, data model, seams, and where each acceptance test attaches) inside the system's architecture, and write it down without writing production code.

plugins.name: implement
plugins.description: Implement authorized work test-first and report its verification evidence.

plugins.name: iterate
plugins.description: Build a living application one verified batch at a time, settling decisions just in time.

plugins.name: review-and-refactor
plugins.description: Review and refactor changes since a fixed point against repository standards and the originating behavior agreement.

plugins.name: specify
plugins.description: Resolve the open decisions about one capability's observable behavior and synthesize its living repository specification: behavior, edge cases, acceptance, and capability requirements.

plugins.name: taskify
plugins.description: Decompose approved work into verifiable tasks with explicit blocking dependencies, locally or on an approved tracker.

plugins.name: test-first
plugins.description: Build features or fix bugs test-first through the red-green loop of test-driven development (TDD), leaving refactoring to a later review.
